non-excepted-horizontal-overflow-at-320p: On a narrow phone-width screen, fixed-width or non-wrapping content spills sideways forcing horizontal scrolling, and a human must judge whether that overflow is a real failure.
f102-content-disappears-no-equivalent: Shrinking the page to phone width hides content (a sidebar, nav links, a search box) with no equivalent way to reach it, so functionality is simply lost.
long-unbreakable-string-overflow-c33: A single long unbroken string like a URL, hash, or API key won't wrap, so it forces sideways scrolling even though the rest of the page reflows fine.
two-d-exception-overclaimed-or-misscoped: Because one table or map legitimately needs sideways scrolling, the developer lets the whole page scroll sideways, so headings and search boxes that should reflow don't.
sticky-fixed-content-consumes-small-view: On a tiny zoomed viewport, sticky headers, footers, cookie bars, or chat widgets eat most of the screen or cover content, leaving almost nothing readable.
carousel-panel-overflow-g225: A sideways-scrolling carousel is allowed, but one over-stuffed panel doesn't fit the narrow width, forcing extra horizontal scrolling inside that single panel.
meaningful-indentation-vs-gratuitous-g22: Code and nested lists may keep meaningful indentation that needs sideways scrolling, but ordinary prose forced not to wrap overflows when it should simply reflow.
